locator.quote: Let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ be the maximum number of $r$-edges that can be placed on $n$ vertices without forming a $K_{r+1}^r$ (the $r$-uniform complete graph on $r+1$ vertices). Is every $r$-hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices the union of at most $\mathrm{ex}_{r}(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ many copies of $K_r^r$ and $K_{r+1}^r$, no two of which share a $K_r^r$?

text.value: For every 3-graph G on n ≤ 9 vertices, |E(G)| − 3ν(G) ≤ ex₃(n, K₄³). Equivalently, every such G admits an edge-disjoint decomposition into at most ex₃(n, K₄³) single triples and tetrahedra.
